If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 2–5% in early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 2–5% in early horizon (1–7 days) to counteract pessimism.  
If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative in mid-horizon (8–15 days), shift forecast downward by 3–7% to reflect sentiment reversal.  
If sentiment remains flat (0.33–0.67) across 5+ days, apply a 1–3% downward bias in late horizon (16–30 days) to account for mean reversion.  
If sentiment is positive but recent prices are trending downward, reduce forecast slope by 1–3% in mid-horizon to align with momentum decay.  
If sentiment is negative but recent prices are trending upward, increase forecast slope by 1–3% in mid-horizon to capture reversal potential.
